# jenkins_node_secret (Ephemeral Resource)

Get the connection secret of an inbound (JNLP) agent node, as passed to `agent.jar -secret`, without storing it in the plan or the state. Requires the Agent/Connect permission on the node.

Use it to feed a write-only argument, such as `secret_string_wo` of `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version`.

Terraform opens an ephemeral resource in both the plan and the apply phase, so a `terraform apply` fetches the secret at least twice, where the `jenkins_node_secret` data source is read once per plan or refresh.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "jenkins_node" "agent" {
  name      = "linux-agent-01"
  remote_fs = "/home/jenkins/agent"
}

# Referencing the node's id defers the lookup until the node exists.
ephemeral "jenkins_node_secret" "agent" {
  name = jenkins_node.agent.id
}

resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "agent" {
  name = "jenkins/agent/linux-agent-01"
}

# A write-only argument (AWS provider 5.90 or later) hands the secret over
# without storing it in the state. Terraform sends it again only when the
# version changes: bump it when the node is renamed or the controller is
# rebuilt from an empty JENKINS_HOME, otherwise the entry keeps the old secret.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "agent" {
  secret_id                = aws_secretsmanager_secret.agent.id
  secret_string_wo         = ephemeral.jenkins_node_secret.agent.secret
  secret_string_wo_version = 1
}
```

Jenkins derives the secret from the node name and a key generated in the controller's `JENKINS_HOME`. It survives restarts and re-applies, and changes only when the node is renamed or the controller is rebuilt from an empty `JENKINS_HOME`. Terraform cannot compare a write-only value with what it sent, so bump the version argument of the receiving resource (`secret_string_wo_version` above) in those two cases.

~> The secret is read from `/computer/<name>/jenkins-agent.jnlp`, an endpoint Jenkins has deprecated. The controller logs a WARNING every time it is fetched: one line per `jenkins_node_secret` for a `terraform plan`, at least two for a `terraform apply`. Jenkins has no supported replacement yet; this ephemeral resource will switch to it once one ships.

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the agent node.

### Read-Only

- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The inbound agent connection secret.
